title: Nearby gauge peaks exceeded land flood depth by 3.38 ft at 37 selected coastal sites in 2017-2024
abstract: We tested the tide-gauge proxy used in a prior NHC surge-range audit against USGS land flood depths. We matched 37 coastal still-water sites in 7 storms to gauges within 10 km. Mean gauge peak water above MHHW exceeded mark height above ground by 3.38 ft. A storm bootstrap gave a conditional 95% interval of 1.58-4.83 ft. Gauge values were greater at 97.3% of sites. Local surveyed water was 0.85 ft higher than gauge water on average, but land was 4.23 ft above the transferred gauge MHHW level. The water and ground effects worked in opposite directions. This is a measurement gap in a selected sample, not an NHC forecast error rate. Survey selection, sparse still-water flags, datum transfer, shared gauges and inherited peak windows limit inference. Paired evidence, code, source hashes and an independent arithmetic check are included.
